q-79337.name: Question 1
q-79337.problem: Let $S$ be a $9\times 12$ matrix that has $7$ pivot columns. What is the dimension of the null space of $S?$
q-79337.worked_solution:
We know that $\text{dim(Null}(S))$ is the number of non-pivot columns in $S.$ 

Since $S$ has $12$ columns and $7$ of them are pivots, then the number of non-pivot columns in $S$ is 

$$
12-7=5.
$$

Therefore, $\text{dim(Null}(S))=5.$

q-79344.name: Question 6
q-79344.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

I. If $B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(B))=3.$

II. If $C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(C))=2.$

III. If $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(A))=0.$
q-79344.worked_solution:
The dimension of the null space of a matrix is the number of non-pivot columns in the matrix. 

Also, all of the given matrices are in row echelon form.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the statements.

- Statement I is false. The matrix $B$ has $3$ pivot columns and no non-pivot columns. So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(B))=0.
$$

- Statement II is false. The matrix $C$ has $2$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $2$nd column). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(C))=1.
$$

- Statement III is true. The matrix $A$ has $2$ pivot columns and no non-pivot columns. So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))=0.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

q-79346.name: Question 7
q-79346.problem:
Consider the matrices given below. Find $\,\text{dim(Null}(A))+\text{dim(Null}(B))+\text{dim(Null}(C)).$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
q-79346.worked_solution:
The dimension of the null space of a matrix is the number of non-pivot columns in the matrix. 

Also, all of the given matrices are in row echelon form.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the statements.

- The matrix $A$ has $2$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $2$nd column). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))=1.
$$

- The matrix $B$ has $1$ pivot column and $1$ non-pivot columns. So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(B))=1.
$$

- The matrix $C$ has $2$ pivot columns and $2$ non-pivot columns (namely, the $2$nd and the $4$th columns). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(C))=2.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))+\text{dim(Null}(B))+\text{dim(Null}(C))=1+1+2=4.
$$

q-139975.name: Question 11
q-139975.worked_solution:
Recall that by definition, $\text{nullity}(W)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(W)).$

To find $\text{dim}(\text{Null}(W))$, we reduce $W$ to row echelon form, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}W & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 & 3 \\ -3 & 12 & 4 & 9 \\ 5 & -20 & 10 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 10 & 18 \\ 5 & -20 & 10 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 10 & 18 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $3$ pivot columns and  $1$
 non-pivot column (the $2$nd). 

Therefore,

$$
\text{nullity}(W)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(W))=1.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & -7 & 9 \\ -3 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ -3 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $3$ pivot columns and no non-pivot columns. 

Therefore,

$$
\text{nullity}(D)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(D))=0.
$$
